record.paper_title: The cosmological constant, dark matter, supersymmetry, and other unsolved problems from a fresh perspective
record.context_brief: Experimental test of the higgson dark matter candidate
record.original_question: Can the predicted lightest higgson h0 dark matter WIMP be confirmed or excluded by direct-detection, collider, or indirect-detection experiments, given the source's stated estimate that it has mass about 70 GeV/c^2, Xe collision cross-section about 10^-48 cm^2, and no non-gravitational interactions except second-order gauge couplings to W and Z bosons?

evidence.quote: For the WIMP predicted by the present theory – the lowest-mass higgson of Section VIII – this cross-section is estimated to be ∼10−48 cm2 [21], with a mass of about 70 GeV/c2, so it may be barely within reach of both LZ and XENONnT.

This particle is unique in that it has precisely defined couplings and a well-defined mass, providing specific cross-sections and other experimental signatures as targets for clean experimental tests.
It has not yet been detected because it has no interactions other than second-order gauge couplings, to W and Z bosons.

artifact.status_search_result: Current xenon-based direct-detection experiments (LZ, XENONnT) have reached spin-independent sensitivities of order 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² for ~30–50 GeV WIMPs as of 2024–2025, approaching but not yet reaching 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 70 GeV. Proposed next-generation detectors (DARWIN/XLZD) aim to probe the 10⁻⁴⁹ cm² regime in the 2030s, after which the neutrino fog becomes the limiting background. No collider or indirect-detection result has confirmed or excluded a 70 GeV WIMP with only loop-level W/Z couplings. The question therefore appears open.

status_evidence.title: LZ First Dark Matter Search Results
status_evidence.snippet: LUX-ZEPLIN reports world-leading limits on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-sections, reaching ~2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near 30 GeV/c² with 4.2 tonne-year exposure.
status_evidence.claim: Current direct-detection sensitivity is approaching but has not yet reached 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 70 GeV/c².

status_evidence.title: XENONnT Dark Matter Search
status_evidence.snippet: XENONnT achieves spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section limits of order 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² for masses near 30 GeV/c².
status_evidence.claim: Existing exclusion limits do not yet cover σ ≈ 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 70 GeV/c².

status_evidence.title: XLZD/DARWIN Design Report
status_evidence.snippet: Next-generation multi-ten-tonne xenon observatories aim at sensitivities down to the neutrino fog near 10⁻⁴⁹ cm².
status_evidence.claim: Reaching 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 70 GeV requires next-generation detectors not yet operational.
